svg.title: Substances & separation
svg.desc: What is the substance?: Element: atoms of one element. Compound: different elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio. Mixture: substances retain chemical properties and can be separated physically. Compounds need chemical reactions. Symbols & equations: H₂O = 2H and 1O; Ca(OH)₂ = 1Ca, 2O, 2H. Use correct upper/lower case in symbols. 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Count each element on both sides; change coefficients only. Binary names often end -ide; -ate names usually include oxygen. Filtration: Separates insoluble solid from liquid. Residue stays on filter; filtrate passes through. Dissolved salt passes through too. Salt + sand: dissolve salt, filter sand, crystallise filtrate. Crystallisation: Partly evaporate solvent → concentrated solution → cool → crystals form. Filter crystals and dry them. Avoid heating hydrated salts strongly to complete dryness. Wear goggles; handle hot glassware carefully. Distillation: Simple: boil liquid, cool vapour in condenser, collect liquid distillate. Recover water from salt solution. Fractional: column gives repeated evaporation/condensation to separate miscible liquids by boiling point. Lower-boiling fraction usually comes first; cooling water enters condenser at bottom. Chromatography: Components have different attractions to solvent and stationary phase, so travel different distances. Pencil baseline above solvent; small spots; mark solvent front. Ink could dissolve; submerged spots wash off. No new substances form in these physical separations.
